restated_task: Implement brackets.core.is_balanced(s), available through from brackets import is_balanced, to return a bool indicating whether all ASCII parentheses, square brackets and curly braces in a string are matched in the correct order and nesting. Ignore every other character, treat the empty string as balanced, and raise TypeError for non-string inputs. Preserve is_bracket and the existing tests.

interface_contract.name: brackets.is_balanced
interface_contract.behavior: Accept a str, including str subclasses. Read bracket characters in order, ignoring all other characters. Each closing bracket must match the most recent unmatched opening bracket: ')' matches '(', ']' matches '[', and '}' matches '{'. Return False if a closing bracket has no matching most recent opening bracket or if any opening brackets remain unmatched at the end; otherwise return True. Return an actual bool on every string input. Quotes, escapes and comments have no special meaning: bracket characters within them still count.
error_cases: TypeError: s is not an instance of str; do not coerce other values to strings.

interface_contract.name: brackets.is_bracket
interface_contract.behavior: Preserve the existing implementation: return True exactly when c is an instance of str of length one and is one of '(', ')', '[', ']', '{', or '}'. Return False otherwise, including for non-string inputs.

acceptance_criteria: 1. from brackets import is_balanced and from brackets import is_bracket continue to succeed.
2. is_balanced returns True for each of '', '()', '[]', '{}', '()[]{}', and '([{}])'.
3. is_balanced returns True for '(a[b]{c})' and 'f(x[0], y[1])'.
4. is_balanced returns False for each of '(', ')', '([)]', '(]', '{[}', and '())'.
5. Unmatched opening brackets of every kind produce False, including '[', '{', and '([]'.
6. Unmatched closing brackets of every kind produce False, including ']', '}', and ')('. Equal numbers of opening and closing brackets alone do not imply balance.
7. Matching requires the correct nesting order at every depth; '([]{})' is True and '{(})' is False.

8. All characters outside the six ASCII bracket characters are ignored. Strings containing only letters, digits, whitespace, punctuation or non-ASCII characters return True, and removing non-bracket characters from any string does not change its result.

9. Quotes and backslashes do not suppress bracket recognition: a string containing a double quote, an opening parenthesis and a double quote returns False, as does a string containing a backslash followed by an opening parenthesis.
10. For every string input, type(is_balanced(s)) is bool, whether the result is True or False.

11. Non-string inputs raise TypeError, including None, True, 0, 1.5, b'()', [], (), {}, and an arbitrary object. Empty non-string values also raise TypeError. No particular exception message is required.
12. Instances of str subclasses are accepted and evaluated using the same bracket-matching rules.
13. Successive calls are independent: calling with '(', then '()', then '' returns False, True, and True.
14. is_bracket remains unchanged: it returns True for each character in '()[]{}' and False for 'a', '', '((', and 1. Existing tests remain unchanged and pass.
out_of_scope: Changing is_bracket, PAIRS, OPEN, CLOSE, or existing package exports.
Recognizing additional bracket types or parsing programming-language syntax, quoted strings, escapes or comments.
Coercing non-string inputs or adding dependencies or public APIs.
Imposing a specific algorithm or performance threshold.
